routes.description: Establish that scientific inquiry and Christian theism are compatible and that a personal rational creator supplies an integrated account of intelligibility, agency, human reason, morality, meaning, fine-tuning, and historically claimed divine action.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if theism can function as a coherent explanatory framework alongside scientific mechanisms, ground the principal features at issue, and support treating distinctively Christian revelation and resurrection claims as evidential questions rather than exclusions imposed by science.

motionBridge.description: Connect scientific intelligibility and the disputed features of human and cosmic reality to a coherent Christian theistic explanation that permits both natural mechanisms and special divine action.

centralBridges.description: Show why an eternal rational source accounts for an intelligible, mathematically ordered universe and truth-directed human cognition more adequately than an unexplained impersonal starting point.
Establish that mechanistic scientific explanations and agent explanations occupy compatible levels, so identifying natural processes does not by itself exclude a creator.
Show that personal revelation, miracles, and resurrection are coherent under theism and can be assessed through historical evidence without treating them as ordinary natural mechanisms.
Explain how a personal God grounds objective moral significance, final justice, enduring meaning, and hope beyond locally constructed purposes.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Relate fine-tuning and cosmic order to purposive agency while distinguishing an evidential design inference from an appeal based solely on unresolved scientific questions.
Clarify how belief in rational creation can support expectations of lawful order and historically motivate investigation of nature.

routes.description: Establish that natural mechanisms, parsimonious physical starting points, anthropic reasoning, and continued inquiry address the relevant phenomena without requiring God, while the specifically Christian claims add unsupported explanatory commitments.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic accounts or warranted research programs remove the need for divine agency across the principal issues and if the additional transition from a possible creator to a personal, morally concerned, miracle-working Christian God remains unestablished.

motionBridge.description: Connect the explanatory sufficiency and open research trajectory of science to rejection of Christian theism as a necessary or adequately supported account of the disputed phenomena.

centralBridges.description: Show how natural selection and impersonal mechanisms explain apparent design and provide a precedent for investigating unresolved origins without invoking divine agency.
Establish that positing a conscious creator adds an explanatorily demanding entity and is unnecessary where physical mechanisms or simpler starting conditions suffice.
Require an evidential bridge from any conceivable cosmic intelligence to incarnation, miracles, resurrection, atonement, and concern with individual human conduct.
Explain how observer selection, lawful conditions, and possible multiverse models can address intelligibility and fine-tuning without inferring a divine mind.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Separate the truth of theistic claims from the desirability of religious comfort, ultimate justice, hope, or existential reassurance.
Identify capacity-, suffering-, and human-construct-based resources for moral reasoning without treating the absence of cosmic justice as proof of divine authority.

sections.title: Scientific Mechanism, Agency, and Apparent Design
sections.rationale: This issue tests the motion's core science-versus-God relationship by asking whether successful mechanistic explanations exclude purposive agency and whether natural selection resolves the principal inference from biological appearance to design.

sections.title: Cosmic Intelligibility, Ultimate Explanation, and Human Reason
sections.rationale: This issue compares rival explanatory starting points for mathematical order, scientific intelligibility, consciousness, and confidence in rational cognition, including disputes over simplicity and brute facts.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Origins, and the Limits of Inquiry
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether fine-tuning and unresolved origins support a design inference or instead call for anthropic reasoning, multiverse possibilities, and continued naturalistic investigation.

sections.title: Christian Revelation, Miracles, and Resurrection
sections.rationale: This issue addresses the required transition from generic creator hypotheses to specifically Christian theism by examining the coherence and evidential status of personal revelation, miracles, incarnation, and resurrection.

sections.title: Morality, Justice, Meaning, and Hope
sections.rationale: This issue compares theistic and naturalistic accounts of objective value, suffering, justice, purpose, and consolation while preserving the distinction between a belief's existential consequences and evidence for its truth.
